project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to construct a new water treatment plant, replacing the existing 65-year-old plant. The new plant will contain a new raw water intake and raw water pumping station. In addition, waterlines will be replaced on Route 20 and Main Street to address the aging and leaking lines. There will also be new fire hydrants installed along these lines to replace or supplement existing fire protection. Approximately 23,000 local rural residents will benefit from the new treatment plant project.

funding_code: CF ARP EMERGENCY RURAL HEALTH CARE GRANTS - TRACK 1 & 2
naics_industry_sector: Health Care and Social Assistance
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be to update the heating, ventilation and air condition (HVAC) system on its inpatient floor. The current system is from 1970 and does not have a negative air exchange which would allow the air to consistently be drawn out of an infected area and not re-circulated to the rest of the non-infected spaces. By updating this HVAC system to include the negative air exchange on the inpatient floor, the patients hospitalized with infectious diseases would be able to stay on the correct floor without potentially infecting other patients. The hospital is currently using the original air mechanical system from 1970 on the inpatient floor. COVID-19 highlighted the issue of air quality and how air exchange can be an effective infection control tool.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development Investment will be used to extend sewer service to the Clarksburg Country Club area and the Laurel Park area. project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used through the ACTAT Program, West Virginia University, University of Kentucky, and University of Tennessee-Knoxville employ various strategies to provide customized technical assistance on-site at water facilities, regional in-person and virtual trainings, and develop and distribute educational materials in their respective states. The regional module trainings will be deployed through an online platform in order to allow multiple utilities to participate. The utility specific training will focus on at least 2 utilities based on results from the regional module trainings and the utility focused assistance will focus on three additional utilities and will provide a more hands-on, technical approach to implement specific goals identified in the regional module training and utility specific training.

Funding will outfit Jefferson High School in Shenandoah Junction, West Virginia and Martinsburg High School in Martinsburg, West Virginia with the technology needed to engage in these distance learning courses and equips the university campus with the hardware necessary to deliver these interactive courses. The university proposes to provide distance learning through synchronous live-streamed dual enrollment courses to over 400 eligible high school students per calendar year.

borrower_name: West Virginia Higher Education Policy Co
funding_code: DLT GRANTS - SUBSTANCE USE DISORDER - EDUCATIONAL
naics_industry_sector: Utilities
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to purchase distance learning equipment that will develop a state-wide network that will provide an interactive telecommunications link between Hub and End users. The project will increase the availability of opioid and substance abuse prevention programs, establish the base of a statewide synchronous interactive distance learning network, expand the availability of college courses to rural communities, improve retention and graduation rates of college students, expand educational opportunities for high schools, improve academic achievement and college readiness for high schools, and increase community resources. The West Virginia Higher Education Policy Commission will serve as the Hub of the project and will serve approximately 5,600 residents in rural West Virginia.

funding_code: DISTANCE LEARNING- GRANT
naics_industry_sector: Utilities
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to provide distance learning technology and telemedicine stations for each of Clay Countys six schools. Distance learning technology will be utilized to provide virtual learning experiences for students across all grade levels, as well as expand opportunities for students to participate in advanced and college level courses not available at their home schools. Telemedicine stations will permit students and their families to confer with medical and mental health professionals at each school-based wellness center. This project will benefit approximately 2,000 residents in Clay County, West Virginia.

funding_code: DISTANCE LEARNING- GRANT
naics_industry_sector: Utilities
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to upgrade telecommunications equipment at seven facilities at Glenville State College in central West Virginia. The equipment will enable the college to connect with dual-credit students at Gilmer County High School, Braxton County High School, Calhoun County High School, Clay County High School, Ridgewood High School and Webster County High School. Funds will also be used to purchase laptops so students can access online classes. In response to the COVID-19 pandemic, the college will establish courses either exclusively online or in a hybrid method in which one portion of the instruction will be delivered on campus and the other portion will be delivered via electronic communications.

borrower_name: Lincoln County Primary Care Center, Inc.
funding_code: DLT GRANTS - CARES ACT - EDUCATIONAL
naics_industry_sector: Utilities
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to implement a distance learning system linking the Lincoln Primary Care Center to 13 sites. The project also is expected to improve the retention of medical staff.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to renovate the Rex Pyles Coliseum at Alderson-Broaddus University. The coliseum houses classrooms, offices, a basketball court, and a swimming pool. It was constructed in the late 1960s and over the past year the four main wood glulam arches that support the roof structure have begun to fail. The facility was closed in February with the classrooms and offices being relocated to other campus buildings. The four arches span the entire building and are each supported at their ends by a concrete thrust block that extends to bedrock. These thrust blocks also act as the collection point for stormwater runoff from the roof. The four main wood glulam arches extend outside the building to these thrust blocks and this is where the wood arches are deteriorating causing the roof structure to settle or drop vertically and sit on non-load bearing masonry walls. In addition, the mezzanine floor and exterior wall structure are seeing loads for which they were not designed.

project_name: 2021 DCI Wastewater Treatment Plant Solids Handling Upgrade Project
funding_code: PERSISTENT POVERTY (COMB LOAN & GRANT) WASTE DISPOSAL ONLY
naics_industry_sector: Utilities
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to make upgrades to the wastewater treatment plant in Fayette County, West Virginia. Upgrades will include two velocity-controlled grit channels, one influent flow meter, and one mechanical and one manual bar screen. Additional upgrades will include one oxidation ditch, two secondary clarifiers, and two chlorine contact chambers. Other upgrades will include one non-potable water system, one post disinfection aeration system, two sludge return and waste pumps, and one liquid sludge holding tank. Additionally, there will be one dewatering building with mechanical sludge dewatering process (centrifuge) and one covered dewatered solids storage and loading area. There will also be two covered sludge drying beds and two drilled potable water wells. They will also add a maintenance building for use as a garage, storage, and disinfection area. One control building will be used as an office, lab, and restroom. There will also be one auxiliary power diesel generator. There will be no changes to the sewer collection system or office building.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will allow the Grant County Public Service District to provide public water and limited fire protection service to 45 new customers in the Knobley Road area and 26 new customers in the Eston Carr Buckbee-Hollow area. The Eston-Carr Buckbee Hollow and Knobley Road areas are plagued with dry and erratic water wells that result in poor quality water, limited farming activities, and lowered property values. The existing water line along Jordan Run is a thin walled polyvinyl chloride pipe that was laid in rocky soil and has continual breaks that drain the maintenance resources of the District.

project_name: Water Intake Dam Emergency Repair Project
funding_code: (GRANT ONLY) ECWAG - APPROPRIATED $1,000,000 LIMIT
naics_industry_sector: Utilities
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to correct a water system failure in the Mill Creek area. The initial Emergency Community Water Assistance Grant closed on November 5, 2019, and when construction commenced in the weeks following, it became apparent the assumed cause of failure was only a small portion of the overall problem. The original proposed project has already constructed a cofferdam 40 feet upstream of the low head dam and dewatered the section of Mill Creek. This revealed that the problem was created due to the dam not being originally tied into competent bedrock for the foundation. Over the years, the force of water had eroded away the foundation leaving supporting wood boards exposed to the creeks elements. After excavation, it was determined that the original repair was not going to work to correct the catastrophic failure. In order to properly resolve the problem, the City of Ripley has proposed the construction of a new low head dam in Mill Creek. This will allow the water to pool high enough in elevation for the water intake screen to operate and fill the raw water wet well. The service area for the City of Ripleys water system is 6,677. There are 4,606 residential customers and 323 commercial customers.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will assist Valley Comprehensive Community Mental Health System in the construction of a new treatment facility in the Pleasant Valley area of Fairmont, West Virginia. The facility will be located on 8.96 acres of land that the System had previously purchased for service expansion. The new facility will expand the Systems current service offering by providing residential treatment and substance use disorder (SUD) services. The residential treatment facility will provide a total of 80 coed beds between two buildings that are gender specific. The female residential treatment building is also capable of accepting women with children for substance abuse treatment. These beds will be used to house clients receiving level 3.5 and 3.1 American Society of Addiction Medicine (ASAM) levels of care. Any excess beds that are not utilized for ASAM Levels of Care will be utilized as Sober Living Beds. The Sober Living Beds provide clients in need with the ability to have longer term extended stays while continuing to receive outpatient SUD Services. The Outpatient SUD services consist of: Intensive Outpatient Therapy, Individual Therapy, Group Therapy, Supportive Individual Counseling, Group Supportive Counseling, Peer Recovery Support Services, Targeted Case Management, Psychiatric Services, Medication Assisted Treatment, Limited Primary Care Services, and Community Focused Treatment. A third Treatment building will be constructed to provide the aforementioned services within close proximity to the two residential buildings. A 16 Bed Crisis Residential Unit (CRU) will also be incorporated within the Treatment Building to provide Substance Abuse Detox Services, Crisis Services, and Hospitalization Step-Down Services.

naics_industry_sector: Utilities
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will help the McDowell County PSD to provide sewer service to 118 potential customers (295 persons) in the Town of Iaeger and the surrounding areas of McDowell County. The proposed project consists of the construction of 15,830 feet of eight-inch and smaller diameter gravity pipe, 7,165 feet of six-inch and smaller diameter force main, and 2,890 feet of four-inch service laterals. The project will also construct four pumping stations, two grinder pumping stations, and one 21,000 gallon per day treatment plant. In addition, there will be one modified existing package treatment facility, 90 manholes, clean-outs, and other related appurtenances. The newly constructed Iaeger Elementary School is the only one of the potential customers in the project area that has its own package treatment facility. According to the McDowell County Health Department, approximately 10 percent of the residents to be served by the project utilize failing private on-site septic systems. The other 90 percent discharge directly into area streams. In multiple areas, sewage is discharged into all community sewer lines which then discharge into Tug Fork and its tributaries. The current sewerage disposal methods in the area are a potential health threat and negatively contribute to the water quality of Tug Fork and its tributaries. This project is necessary to correct the current situation and will protect local water supplies.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to extend 3,000 feet of four-inch and six-inch water line and install a fire hydrant and a below ground pressure-reducing station along Gillespie Road. This project will provide water service to an additional 14 customers. Additionally, approximately 5,000 feet of three-inch water line along Halleck Road will be replaced with four-inch and six-inch water line. The system maintains 50 miles of main water distribution lines, six water storage tanks, and five booster stations. This project will serve approximately 2,392 residents.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used by the City of Paden City for emergency water treatment plant upgrades. The City will remove their existing three hydraulic venturi air strippers. Only two of the three strippers are operational, and the City can only operate one stripper at a time due to pressure constraints. With the condition of the existing strippers, the City cannot effectively treat the tetrachloroethylene (PCE) contamination in the groundwater. They plan to replace all three strippers with a new six-tray EZ Tray 1000 gallons per minute air stripper. Work will also include the necessary piping, electrical, and building upgrades to install the new air stripper. The new air stripper is designed to treat the highest influent levels of PCE experienced at the existing water treatment plant with an added factor of safety. QED Environmental Systems has modeled the influent level and is able to predict the effectiveness of the air stripper at these levels. It was determined that the selected air stripper could treat the highest tested influent levels with 100 percent effectiveness. These additional Emergency Community Water Assistance Grant funds were needed to complete the project. Construction will begin soon after closing in December 2019. This project will benefit the 2,621 residents of the City.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will allow Ravencliff-McGraws-Saulsville Public Service District to develop and utilize a new raw water source. The new source is the abandoned underground workings of the Ranger Fuel Beckley No. 2 Mine. The water reserve will be accessed via the abandoned Sabine air shaft. The water is roughly 500 feet deep in the air shaft, meaning that the entire abandoned mine is flooded. The water quality has been tested and is more than adequate for a public water supply. After completion of the project, the PSD will have a permanent, adequate raw source to meet its customers needs well into the future. The PSD provides fresh water to over 1200 customers, including a nursing home, high school, state park, elementary school, and community college. It was projected that the District would be without water within the next three months if a new source was not accessed.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will enable Greater Harrison Public Service District (PSD) to extend sewer service to the Clarksburg Country Club area and the Laurel Park area. It will include roughly 85,385 LF of new line of various diameters. Some of the new line will be gravity and some will be force main. This section will also include 180 manholes, five duplex lift stations, three duplex grinder lift stations, and seven grinder pumps. The sewage from this new collection system will be treated at the PSDs existing wastewater treatment plant at West Milford. The Rt. 73 Section of the project includes about 62,470 LF of various diameter new line both gravity and force main as well as a new 100,000 GPD Orbal oxidation ditch wastewater treatment plant near Boothsville. The new plant will include two bar screens, grit removal, disc aerators, two clarifiers, ultraviolet disinfection, aerated sludge holding tank and other appurtenances. There will also be 228 manholes and three duplex grinder stations. This project will serve an estimated 747 new customers. This additional grant for $2,000,000 will complete this project.

funding_code: (GRANT ONLY) WATER ONLY
naics_industry_sector: Utilities
project_announced_description: This USDA investment will consist of constructing 32,860 linear feet of waterline, one 150,000 gallon water storage tank, one booster station, two pressure reducing stations, 16 fire hydrants, and other related work. The proposed water system facilities are in the Brushfork area along Route 52, Airport Road, Mowles Chapel Road, and Stoney Gap Road and will provide public water and fire hydrant coverage to 75 new customers. The residents and businesses currently use wells and cisterns which do not provide safe and adequate supplies of potable water. The businesses at the Mercer County Airport are experiencing major problems with their well water supply sources. These well water sources have almost dried up and do not have sufficient water to provide the basic potable water needs for the airport and other businesses located at the airport. The airport is currently hauling water as a temporary measure. In addition to providing safe potable water to the proposed new customers, the project will also improve water system pressure to 30 existing customers and provide fire hydrant coverage to 100 existing water customers. These subsequent grant funds in the amount of $250,000.00 were needed to complete this project.

naics_industry_sector: Utilities
project_announced_description: This USDA investment will be used by the City of Paden City to remove their existing hydraulic venturi air strippers and replace them with a new six tray EZ- Tray 1000 GPM Air Stripper. Work will also include the necessary piping, electrical and building upgrades to install the new air stripper. The new air stripper is designed to treat the highest influent levels of perchloroethylene experienced (PCE) at the existing water treatment plant (WTP) with an added factor of safety. QED Environmental has modeled the influent level and is able to predict the effectiveness of the air stripper at these levels. It was determined that the selected air stripper could treat the highest tested influent levels with 100% effectiveness. The City currently has three hydraulic venturi air strippers installed at the WTP. Only two of the three strippers are operational and the City can only operate one stripper at a time due to pressure constraints. With the condition of the existing air strippers, the City cannot effectively treat the PCE contamination in the groundwater.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to address an unreliable, older portion of the Ravencliff-McGraws-Saulsville Public Service Districts water system in the New Richmond Water System. Upgrades will include adding fencing to booster stations at Twin Falls, Glen Fork, and Saulsville; repairing tank gauges for McGraws, Sabine and Saulsville tanks; repainting McGraws Tank No. 1; installing new filter media in three filters at the water treatment plant; renovating the flow control building; paying off an emergency tank rehabilitation loan in the amount of $80,000; and purchasing a new backhoe to assist in maintaining the system. This water distribution and water treatment system serves approximately 927 residential customers and one commercial customer. Previous Rural Development funding was a 40-year loan for $1,673,000 at 2.625% and a grant for $750,000. Other funds included $440,000 from the West Virginia Infrastructure and Jobs Development Council.
